subject.title: [Bug]: Isolated cron agentTurn fails with 'setup timed out before runner start' — all fallback models exhausted on 2026.5.12

question: Should OpenClaw accept a longer derived isolated-cron setup watchdog for long agentTurn jobs, require an operator config knob, or preserve the 60s ceiling?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but automation should not choose the product tradeoff between fewer false setup aborts and longer cron-capacity occupancy when setup is genuinely stuck.

options.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
options.body: Merge or sponsor the PR path that keeps a 60s floor, caps setup time, and derives the setup budget from the job timeout.

options.title: Require explicit config knob
options.body: Ask for an operator-controlled cron setup watchdog setting and matching docs/schema proof before changing the default behavior.

options.title: Keep 60s and improve diagnostics only
options.body: Preserve the short stuck-setup ceiling and focus follow-up work on attribution, provider-specific cold starts, or restart recovery.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded derived watchdog
recommendation.body: Merge or sponsor the PR path that keeps a 60s floor, caps setup time, and derives the setup budget from the job timeout.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the merged cron pre-model watchdog diagnostics that established this timeout boundary and is the strongest routing candidate for the behavior tradeoff.
